title: Show the no-edge irreducible bound fails in pattern dimension 4.
body: ## Change and mathematical scope The no-edge irreducible joint-image bound does not stay 3 in pattern dimension 4. For every ambient width W ≥ 4, the four projectors ```text N_i = e_i (e_i + e_{i+1} + e_{i+2})^T, i in Z/4Z, ``` are the complete pool of their off-diagonal pattern span. That span has dimension 4 and contains no matrix unit. The joint image has dimension 4 and the action is irreducible. This is an existence result under the same hypotheses as #6921: a complete noncoordinate rank-one idempotent pool over F2 with no matrix unit. It is not an upper bound at pattern dimension 4, and it is not a classification of every such pool. It is not a paid-profile improvement and **no new κ** is claimed. The selected value stays `781451/250000000`. The width-6 parity pool from #6838 has pattern dimension 4 and total image 5, but its image has a four-dimensional invariant kernel. That pool is reducible and does not answer the question. The dimension-at-most-3 theorem of #6921 is cited and not reproved. ## Task and overlap Base commit: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`. This fork PR is based on the existing pin `cursor/crocswap-main-7c49fe32-1dbb` of that commit. Fork `main` is not upstream main. Card `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 8. Scope status: **changed**. The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. The actual result answers open question 2 of #6921. No new alphabet or word is built. The original native acceptance gate remains unmet. Question 1 of #6921, paid-rank accounting after a relation split, is not this result. Nearest work: - #6921 proves the bound 3 for pattern dimension at most 3 and leaves dimension 4 open. Its Fano-plane case split is not reused. - #6838 supplies the total-image bound 4 for pattern dimension at most 3, cited not reproved, and the parity scope control rechecked here as reducible. - #6785 is a one-edge exclusion. #6782 is an edge-quotient bound. #5921 supplies the fiber lemma; this proof does not depend on it. Overlap search on 2026-11-10 covered 885 open PRs and 6934 discussion records. The only records containing this question are #6921 and discussion comment 19474334. Both leave it open. No match is not a novelty certificate; the distinctions above are from reading those records. ## Validation Python 3.12, standard library only. From the repository root: ```sh python3 -B research/pattern-dim4-irreducible-image/verify.py python3 -I -O -B research/pattern-dim4-irreducible-image/verify.py python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pattern-dim4-irreducible-image ``` Observed: `PASS_PATTERN_DIM4_IRREDUCIBLE_IMAGE` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The verifier repeats the covector row reduction, all sixteen pattern weights, the six plane pairs, the complete pool at widths 4 through 8, and the full subspace lattice of F2^4 (67 subspaces, matching the Gaussian counts). Negative controls: deleting one cycle projector leaves an invariant line; the #6921 sharp triple stays irreducible; the normal-form triple stays reducible; the parity pool matches the #6838 width-6 witness and has a four-dimensional kernel. Those finite checks do not replace the all-width support casework in `PROOF.md`, and they do not enumerate every four-dimensional pattern space. No Lean, Docker, or historical replay was run. The selected baseline was not rerun. ## Credit Nick Petalas, #5921, for the fiber lemma and the joint-image question. CubeJerry, #6838, for the total-image bound and the parity pool. #6921 isolated this dimension-4 question and proved the bound for pattern dimension at most 3. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. New work is Apache-2.0. ## Open next questions 1. Can a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 act irreducibly on a joint image of dimension 5 or more? The four-cycle attains 4, so bound 3 fails, but it gives no replacement ceiling. The parity pool attains total dimension 5 and is reducible. First give one explicit pool with a written invariant-subspace check, or prove an upper bound under these same hypotheses. No support reduction here makes an exhaustive search finite, so a search that finds nothing would not be a proof. ## Workflow feedback (optional) The overlap cache separates this scalar question from unrelated four-cycle graph and centre-graph results. One link to the feedback discussion is enough: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
